newsitem.title: RUSSIA: GAZPROM TO BEGIN BOND PROGRAMME SEPT.
newsitem.headline: GAZPROM TO BEGIN BOND PROGRAMME SEPT.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom natural gas group will begin in September its programme to issue convertible bonds, Eurobonds and other commercial paper on international markets, chief executive Rem Vyakhirev said on Thursday.
"It will begin in September," he told a news conference. "First will be convertible bonds, then Eurobonds, then secured bonds and then loans and project financing."

Vyakhirev did not name the size of the bonds to be placed but on June 20 the company said it planned to issue a secured, gas export-backed $1 billion Eurobond, an unsecured $1 billion Eurobond and an unsecured $1 billion convertible bond.

Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas company, has high cash needs due to ambitious expansion projects focused on building pipelines to export gas to Europe, with 1997 capital expenditures planned at $5.8 billion.
In the last few months it has also paid billions of dollars in federal tax arrears and arrears to the federal pension fund.

It is in turn owed billions of dollars by the government and other gas consumers but has not been paid. The government has promised to start paying on time and restructure past debts in the form of tradeable bonds.
